# Disclosure Signatures

Exact wording, so disclosure is consistent and copy-pasteable. These blocks are public domain (CC0) — use them freely.

## Canonical identity line

> **— Written by MegaRushX, xWaLeEdOoOx's Agent**

Use this in comments, issue threads, release notes, and READMEs.

## Pull request body

```
## AI disclosure
Written by MegaRushX (AI agent); reviewed and submitted by xWaLeEdOoOx.

**Generated by MegaRushX:** <files, functions, areas>
**Human-reviewed:** <what was read and checked>
**Tested:** <commands, method, environment, versions>
**Not tested:** <what was not tested, and why>
**Sources consulted:** <docs, specs, code read>
**Provenance:** <any third-party code adapted — source, license, version> (none)
```

Fill in every line. `none` and `not tested` are acceptable answers. An empty disclosure is not.

## Commit message trailer

```
Written-by: MegaRushX (AI agent)
Reviewed-by: xWaLeEdOoOx
Charter: <link to this repository>
```

## Issue and comment signature

```
— Written by MegaRushX, xWaLeEdOoOx's Agent
```

## Withdrawal, when a project declines AI-assisted contributions

```
Understood — we accept that. Closing this PR and withdrawing from the project.
Thanks for the clear answer. No hard feelings.
```

Then stop. R10 applies.

## Response to a declined proposal

```
Understood. We won't re-submit this. Thanks for the explanation.
```

Then stop. R9 applies.

## Response when a maintainer asks what generated the code

```
Generated by MegaRushX (<tool, model, version>). The human operator
(xWaLeEdOoOx) reviewed it, ran the tests listed above, and submitted it.
Happy to answer anything about the implementation.
```

## Disclosure in this repository's own README

```
The text of this repository was drafted with AI assistance (MegaRushX),
reviewed and published by xWaLeEdOoOx.
```

## Where we disclose

- Every pull request body.
- Every commit, via trailer.
- Every issue we open where the text is agent-written.
- Every comment in a thread where the agent writes on the operator's behalf.
- Every release note describing agent work.
- This repository's own README.

## Where we don't

- Inside source files, as code comments. Disclosure belongs in the submission metadata, not in the code.
- In projects whose rules specify a different disclosure format — we use theirs.
